Everything on this page is free to use. Know a great resource we've missed? [Tell us](join.qmd#write).

## Getting started

[R from CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/)
: Download and install R itself, for Windows, macOS or Linux.

[RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) or [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/)
: Editors that make writing R code much easier. Install R first.

[Posit Cloud](https://posit.cloud/)
: Run R in your web browser, with nothing to install.

[Your first steps in R](posts/2026-11-13-first-steps-in-r/index.qmd)
: Our own 30-minute tutorial for complete beginners.

[swirl](https://swirlstats.com/)
: Learn R interactively, inside R itself.

## Free online books

[R for Data Science (2nd edition)](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/)
: The standard introduction to importing, cleaning, exploring and visualising data with the tidyverse.

[Hands-On Programming with R](https://rstudio-education.github.io/hopr/)
: Learn to program in R through small, practical projects.

[The Epidemiologist R Handbook](https://www.epirhandbook.com/)
: A practical reference for public health and epidemiology work, written by and for field epidemiologists.

[ggplot2: Elegant Graphics for Data Analysis](https://ggplot2-book.org/)
: Everything you need to make clear, beautiful charts.

[Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/)
: Working with maps and spatial data.

[Tidy Modeling with R](https://www.tmwr.org/)
: Statistical modelling and machine learning with the tidymodels packages.

[Mastering Shiny](https://mastering-shiny.org/)
: Build interactive web apps and dashboards in R.

[Advanced R](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/) and [R Packages](https://r-pkgs.org/)
: For when you're ready to go deeper and share your own code.

[Big Book of R](https://www.bigbookofr.com/)
: A searchable collection of hundreds of free R books, sorted by topic.

## Courses and lessons

[Data Carpentry](https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/)
: Free, community-written lessons that teach data skills to researchers, with several R lessons.

[Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/)
: Create reports, slides and websites (like this one) from your R code.

## Tanzanian and regional data

Practise with data about the places and questions you care about.

[National Bureau of Statistics (NBS)](https://www.nbs.go.tz/)
: Official Tanzanian statistics, including census and survey reports.

[The DHS Program](https://dhsprogram.com/)
: Demographic and Health Surveys, including several rounds for Tanzania. Free registration is required to download data.

[World Bank Open Data](https://data.worldbank.org/country/tanzania)
: Development indicators for Tanzania and every other country. The [WDI](https://cran.r-project.org/package=WDI) package downloads them straight into R.

[Humanitarian Data Exchange](https://data.humdata.org/group/tza)
: Open datasets on Tanzania from humanitarian and development organisations.

## Communities

[AfricaR](https://africa-r.org/)
: A network connecting R users and groups across Africa.

[R-Ladies](https://rladies.org/)
: A worldwide organisation promoting gender diversity in the R community.

[rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org/)
: Open tools and a welcoming community for research software.

[Posit Community](https://forum.posit.co/)
: A friendly forum for questions about R, RStudio, Shiny and more.

[R Weekly](https://rweekly.org/)
: A weekly round-up of R news, tutorials and packages.
